messages.subject: convergence between lavaaan and Amos
parts:

Richard

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: convergence between lavaaan and Amos
parts: There may be small differences between packages, including the use of n or n - 1 to compute covariances or standard errors, and also differences in "tuning," which may lead different programs to converge on slightly different values for the same data and model. AFAIK, lavaan does not currently include a "mimic" option to better match Amos results.

messages.author: 8e48c444b9a8fd35
messages.subject: Re: convergence between lavaaan and Amos
parts:
Dear Prof Rosseel,

Thank you so much for your help ! As I already say:
- RMSEA are equivalent
- SRMR too
- standardized loading between ov and lv too
... but not the standardized regression weights between latent variables


My R code:

library (lavaan)

model <- 'SB =~ SB2+ SB3+ SB4+ SB8 
          SC =~ SC1 + SC2 + SC3 + SC4 + SC5 + SC8 
          SL =~ SL1 + SL3 + SL4 + SL5 
          AM =~ AM1 + AM2 + AM7 + AM8

          SL ~ SB + SC + AM
          SC ~ SB + AM
          SB ~ AM '


fit <- sem (model, data = ame, estimator = "ML")
summary (fit, fit.measures = T)
standardizedSolution(fit)
modindices(fit)


Prof Richard Ladwein
